title: Surveillance Index: Edition One
format: Softcover, supplied in a tote bag

description.main: Surveillance Index Edition One is a reference index of one hundred books on surveillance photography, compiled from Mark Ghuneim's collection.
description.extended:
Surveillance Index: Edition One is a printed reference to one hundred books on surveillance photography, assembled by the collector Mark Ghuneim from his own library.

Each book is indexed by year, title, photographer, description, size and code, with a representative spread and a short text for every entry. It includes a poster showing all of the books and comes in a black tote bag. An essay by Carlo McCormick, "The Eyes Have It", covers the history of surveillance and its precedents in art. The printed index accompanies an online version at surveillanceindex.com. In January 2018 the Paris photography space Le Bal opened its Performing Books programme with the collection, showing more than 200 titles from it.

Ghuneim describes himself on the project site as an internet entrepreneur who began collecting books by artists and photographers about watchers and the watched in 2009. Le Bal's programme notes say he catalogued New York's street CCTV cameras with the ACLU in the early 1990s. A second edition of 111 further books was curated in 2017 and is to be added to the site.

notes: Author is Mark Ghuneim, who appears to be the library's owner (the site and the catalogue's home page publication card are the same project); confirm before cataloguing under his name. Identity confirmed from surveillanceindex.com home page (fetched) and Twelve Books listing. No ISBN found (self-published; Twelve Books lists none). YEAR CONFLICT: Twelve Books says 2016; the site's Le Bal notice (Jan 2018) says 'his self-published 2017 book'. 2017 used, flagged. Pages 324 and 280 x 355 mm come from Twelve Books only. The cover is portrait (600x764), so 355 mm is height. Twelve Books also says 'special-edition bookmark' and later 'new black and silver tote bags' (11/01/2019 site news), so bag/extras vary by printing. Twelve Books Japan copies distributed 2020. Library holds multiple copies: catalogue as one record. The 'Surveillance Index' catalogue tag plausibly marks books indexed in this project. No page states the tag rule. No prices recorded.
